research_question: How is the effort to escape critical-mineral supply chokepoints turning the deep ocean into a geopolitical and legal frontier before ecological risk and commercial viability are settled?
working_thesis: Deep-sea mining is accelerating because governments and companies want strategic control over mineral supply chains. Japan's rare-earth-mud programme, the United States' national permitting route and the unresolved ISA mining code show technology and security policy moving faster than shared governance and ecological certainty.

claims.claim: Japan continuously lifted rare-earth mud from three layers at a pipe depth of 5,569 metres during its 2026 Minamitorishima test.
limitations: Technical success is not proof of commercial viability or reserve scale.

claims.claim: Japan plans a roughly one-month integrated mining-to-processing trial beginning in February 2027 and an industrial/economic assessment by March 2028.
Limited test samples were reported to contain a high share of medium and heavy rare earths, strengthening the project's strategic relevance.
limitations: Keep the 54% figure attributed to Reuters and state that deposit amount and extent were not disclosed.

claims.claim: China's dominance is greatest not only in mining but in rare-earth refining and magnet manufacturing.
limitations: Use magnet-rare-earth scope and 2024 dates explicitly.

claims.claim: Chinese export controls in 2025 turned supply concentration into factory-level disruption outside China.
limitations: Do not imply permanent total cutoff.

claims.claim: The case for seabed minerals cannot be reduced to 'the green transition needs them': cobalt demand growth has moderated with LFP batteries, while rare-earth and processing chokepoints remain strategically acute.
limitations: Scenario-based; avoid claiming any mineral is unnecessary.

claims.claim: As of the end of the ISA Council's July 2026 meetings, commercial exploitation rules remained unfinished and moved into a roadmap and further intersessional work.
limitations: Recheck immediately before script lock because negotiations continue.

claims.claim: UNCLOS defines the seabed beyond national jurisdiction and its resources as the common heritage of mankind.
limitations: Legal implications of U.S. action are disputed and must be attributed.

claims.claim: The United States is pursuing a national DSHMRA permitting route for parts of the international seabed while not being a party to UNCLOS.
limitations: Do not state that a commercial permit has already been issued.

claims.claim: NOAA's compliance determination for TMC's application was a procedural milestone, not approval of a licence or commercial recovery permit.
limitations: Status may change; recheck before narration lock.

claims.claim: Physical disturbance and altered communities remained visible 44 years after a small 1979 collector test, although some organisms recolonized.
limitations: Historical small test and older machinery; not a direct commercial-scale forecast.

claims.claim: Two months after a 2022 industrial-scale trial, density and species richness were lower inside mining tracks and plume-affected communities showed altered dominance relationships.
limitations: Short follow-up; distinguish track effects from plume-area findings.

claims.claim: A monitored collector plume travelled kilometres but was strongest close to the seabed and declined sharply with distance, height and time.
limitations: Do not simplify this into either 'plumes stay local' or 'plumes poison the whole ocean.'

claims.claim: Proposed discharge particles could disrupt midwater food webs by diluting nutritious natural particles.
limitations: Potential mechanism, not observed commercial-scale collapse.

claims.claim: Proponents argue nodules can avoid some land disturbance, tailings and selected lifecycle impacts associated with terrestrial ores.
limitations: Corporate/commissioned evidence; lifecycle categories do not settle deep-sea biodiversity loss.

research_gaps: Final outcome of the ISA Assembly and any post-July 2026 Council decisions
Full publicly releasable TMC USA A application and EIS schedule
Independent economic model for Minamitorishima rare-earth mud
Processing location, waste stream and energy intensity for Japan's 2027 trial
Commercial-scale cumulative plume and noise impacts across multiple collector vehicles
How benefit-sharing would work for developing states under a future ISA code
Whether changing battery chemistry materially weakens the business case for CCZ nodules by the planned production date
